set.lua.err.targetType: This result type is not allowed for LUA.

set.lua.fn.continent: true if the client is on the continent (geo)
set.lua.fn.country: true if the client is in the country (geo)
set.lua.fn.ifportup: Addresses whose TCP port is reachable
set.lua.fn.ifurlup: Addresses whose URL check succeeds (groups = failover levels)
set.lua.fn.netmask: true if the client is in one of the networks
set.lua.helpExpr: A single expression is evaluated directly, as if preceded by return.
set.lua.helpLines: Line breaks become spaces when saving, so do not use -- comments.
set.lua.helpQuotes: Put strings in the code in single quotes ('…') or [[…]] – double quotes are not allowed.
set.lua.helpResult: The result must match the result type: an IP or a list of IPs for A/AAAA, a text for TXT, a host name for CNAME.
set.lua.helpStatements: Several statements: start the code with ; and return the result with return.
set.lua.import.blocked: LUA records are disabled in this panel – this file cannot be imported.
set.lua.import.enableHint: They are only served if enable-lua-records is active on the servers.
set.lua.import.issues: Issues in LUA lines (PowerDNS validates on import itself):
set.lua.notAllowedAdmin: Only administrators may create or change LUA records.
set.lua.notAllowedDisabled: LUA records are disabled in this panel.
set.lua.settings.enableHint: To enable LUA on a PowerDNS server, add enable-lua-records=yes to pdns.conf and restart PowerDNS.
set.lua.settings.intro: Choose who may create and change LUA records. Deleting is always possible with write access to the zone.
set.lua.settings.policyAdminDesc: LUA code runs on the DNS servers – only admins may create or change it.
set.lua.settings.policyDisabledDesc: Nobody can create or change LUA records; zone files containing LUA are rejected on import. Existing records stay and can be deleted.
set.lua.settings.policyManage: Everyone with write access to the zone
set.lua.settings.policyManageDesc: Zone managers and matching API tokens may maintain LUA records – including health checks against any address.
set.lua.settings.title: LUA records
set.lua.statusNoGeoip: {{server}}: geoip backend not loaded – geo functions find nothing there
set.lua.tableNotActive: LUA is not enabled on {{servers}} – these records are not evaluated there.
set.lua.templateReplaceConfirm: Replace the existing code with the template?
set.lua.templates.continent.desc: Clients from Europe get their own address (needs geoip).
set.lua.templates.continent.label: Answer by continent
set.lua.templates.country.desc: Clients from DE, AT and CH get their own address (needs geoip).
set.lua.templates.country.label: Answer by country
set.lua.templates.ifportup.desc: Returns only addresses whose TCP port is reachable.
set.lua.templates.ifportup.label: Failover via port check (IPv4)
set.lua.templates.ifportup6.desc: Same as above, for AAAA answers.
set.lua.templates.ifportup6.label: Failover via port check (IPv6)
set.lua.templates.ifurlup.desc: Checks a URL; answers from the second group if no address of the first one is up.
set.lua.templates.ifurlup.label: Failover via HTTP check
set.lua.templates.latlon.desc: Shows the coordinates PowerDNS determines for the client – useful to test geoip.
set.lua.templates.latlon.label: Client location as TXT
set.lua.templates.pickclosest.desc: Picks the address geographically closest to the client (needs geoip).
set.lua.templates.pickclosest.label: Closest server
set.lua.templates.pickwrandom.label: Weighted distribution
set.lua.templates.view.desc: Internal networks get an internal address, everyone else the public one.
set.lua.templates.view.label: Answer by client network
set.lua.warn.backslash: PowerDNS passes backslashes (\) to Lua unchanged – only use them if you are sure.
set.lua.warn.lineComment: The code contains --. Since line breaks become spaces, a comment would disable the rest of the code.
set.lua.warnEnable: PowerDNS only evaluates LUA records if every server that serves the zone has enable-lua-records=yes (or shared) in pdns.conf. Otherwise clients get no usable answer.
set.lua.warnExec: The code runs on the DNS server for every query. Health checks such as ifportup and ifurlup open connections from there to the given addresses and URLs.
set.lua.warnGeo: Geo functions (pickclosest, country, continent, latlon …) need the geoip backend with a GeoIP database on the PowerDNS server. The panel offers geo records only through these LUA functions.
set.lua.warnSecondary: Secondaries that are not PowerDNS with LUA enabled cannot answer LUA records.
set.lua.warnTitle: LUA records – please read before saving

set.zoneDetail.hintLUA:
Dynamic record: PowerDNS runs Lua code for every query and returns the result as the result type.
Format: <result type> "<Lua code>"
Example: A "ifportup(443, {'192.0.2.1', '192.0.2.2'})"
